title: Polynomial certificates from products of delocalization denominators
statement: Let $R,A,\Lambda$ be commutative rings, with $A$ and $\Lambda$ algebras over $R$, and let $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Let $S\subset R$ be a multiplicative submonoid and use localization at its images [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Fix nonnegative integers $n,t,m,c$ with $c\le n+m$, and a presentation $P$ of $A$ with generators $p_i$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}n$), relations $g_j\in R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}t$), and kernel generated by these relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $D$ be an $S^{-1}R$-algebra, $Q$ a standard smooth presentation of $D$ with $n+m$ variables and $c$ relations whose initial Jacobian minor is a unit [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\beta}D\xrightarrow{\gamma}S^{-1}\Lambda$ a factorization of $S^{-1}\alpha$. Suppose that the first $n$ variables of $Q$ represent $\beta(p_i/1)$. Put $T=R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n+m-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], write $\widetilde g_j$ for $g_j$ with variables included as the first $n$, and use polynomial partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Then there exist $F_j\in T$ for $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(c+t)$, $l_i\in\Lambda$ for $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+m)$, $s\in S$, and $b\in T$, such that $l_i=\alpha(p_i)$ for $i<n$, $F_{c+j}=\widetilde g_j$ for $j<t$, every $F_j$ evaluates to zero at $l$, $C(s)-b\Delta(F)\in(F_0,\ldots,F_{c+t-1})$, and $C(s)F_j\in(F_0,\ldots,F_{c-1})$ for every $j\ge c$. Here $\Delta(F)=\det(\partial F_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j<c}$ and $C$ is the constant inclusion $R\to T$.

proof.text: Apply the denominator-data lemma. Define F by its first c scaled equations C(sf_j) f_j and last t renamed original relations g_j; define ug=product sg_j, uf=product sf_j, s=s_0 ug uf, and replace a_0 by C(ug) a_0.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: The scaled equations evaluate to zero by the denominator data. For each remaining relation, evaluation at l equals alpha applied to evaluation of g_j at the generators of P, which is zero.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: For each k, C(uf) f_k belongs to the ideal of scaled equations, by multiplying C(sf_k) f_k by the product over the other sf factors. Span induction therefore shows that C(uf) multiplies every polynomial in (f) into this ideal.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: Differentiate C(sf_j) f_j using R-linearity of each partial derivative. Multilinearity of the determinant gives Delta(F)=C(uf) Delta(f). Multiply the identity for s_0 by C(ug) C(uf); its error term is in the scaled-equation ideal by the preceding step. This is the asserted Jacobian congruence.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: Apply span induction to C(sg_j) g_j in (f), then multiply by C(s_0) times the product of the other sg factors. The result is C(s) g_j in the initial scaled-equation ideal. Every index after c is one of these g_j; no initial index is at least c.
